title: Minimax sample complexity of proper agnostic online reinforcement learning
formal: Editorial quantitative finite-state variant: determine, up to universal constant factors, the minimax episodic sample complexity N(Pi,H,epsilon) for proper agnostic online reinforcement learning in the model below, uniformly over all finite deterministic policy classes Pi and 0<epsilon<1/2.
definitions:
An instance description specifies a horizon H≥1, finite nonempty disjoint state layers S1,…,SH, a designated initial state s0 in S1, a fixed action set {0,1}, and a nonempty finite class Pi of deterministic policies. A policy is a table assigning one action to every state; the layer identifies time. The learner receives all these tables. The unknown MDP has arbitrary stochastic transitions from layer h to h+1, and a terminal reward in [0,1] whose distribution depends on the last state and action. Earlier rewards are zero. All probability distributions may have arbitrary real probabilities. The value V(pi) is expected terminal reward from s0.

Each episode starts afresh at s0 and follows the actual transitions for H steps. The learner observes visited states, chosen actions and the terminal reward. During training it may choose arbitrary randomized actions based on the entire history, including previous episodes. It cannot reset to an intermediate state, sample a chosen transition or inspect the transition/reward tables. There is no computation or policy-evaluation cost restriction: this is statistical complexity with measurable randomized learning rules.

N(Pi,H,epsilon) is the least nonnegative integer N for which some such rule, after at most N complete episodes, outputs a member pi-hat of Pi with V(pi-hat)≥max over Pi of V(pi) minus epsilon with probability at least 2/3, for every MDP on these layers. The layer sets and start state are understood as part of Pi’s description. N is finite, since testing every policy separately is allowed.

The required answer supplies an explicit expression or structural parameter g of the policy tables, layers, H and epsilon, and universal constants c,C>0 with c g≤N+1≤C g for every description. A definition merely repeating the optimization over learners and MDPs is not a determination. The added one handles classes learnable without samples. This narrows the broad characterization request to a specified minimax quantity; dependence on state count is not prohibited in the expression. It fixes proper output, binary actions and terminal rewards rather than silently treating all online RL models as equivalent.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked characterization with matching upper and lower sample bounds within universal constant factors. Its upper bound must use episodic online access and proper output. A generative-model characterization or an unmatched necessary condition is insufficient; the numerical 1/100 convention is not applied to this asymptotic comparison.
context:
Jia and coauthors distinguish generative access from online interaction: a policy-class parameter sufficient in the former does not characterize the latter. Additional structure yields online upper bounds.

The present finite-state minimax formulation is an editorial sharpening of that broad structural research direction, with proper output explicitly retained from the imported card.
why: A structural characterization would distinguish statistically tractable online reinforcement learning from settings needing stronger access.

import_provenance.original_statement: Which finite policy classes Π permit learning an ε-optimal member in every unknown horizon-H MDP using only poly(H, log|Π|, 1/ε) online episodes, for a fixed finite action set? Rakhlin and collaborators showed that bounded spanning capacity suffices with a generative model but not online; a necessary-and-sufficient characterization is missing.
